    Travelling in

    Smaller than Ireland, with two monsoons, eight World Heritage Sites and a beach in season every month.

    The places locals keep

    1. Pidurangala Rock

      The last ten minutes are a boulder scramble. Start in darkness at about 5:15 with a head-torch to hold a place on the summit for sunrise.

    2. Ritigala forest monastery

      Local legend says the mountain is a piece of the Himalaya that Hanuman dropped while carrying herbs, which is why healing plants grow here.

    3. Yapahuwa

      Those staircase lions once appeared on the 10-rupee note. Almost no tour buses stop here.

    4. Aukana Buddha

      The name is often read as "sun-eating": the statue faces east and is at its best in the first light. A raindrop from its nose is said to fall exactly between its feet.

    5. Ambuluwawa Tower

      The complex holds a Buddhist stupa, a Hindu kovil, a mosque and a church side by side. Skip the final spiral in wind or rain; turn back if it feels wrong.

    6. Knuckles Range and Riverston

      Pitawala Pathana is the "mini World's End": a 20-minute walk to a drop as dramatic as Horton Plains, without the crowd. Swim at Bambarakiri Ella just off the road.

    7. Meemure

      Stay a night. The Lakegala climb with a village guide gives a view across the whole Knuckles range.

    8. Diyaluma Falls

      Take the village path to the upper pools (about 45 min). The rock is slick after rain; stay in the middle pools, away from the lip.

    Leopard, whale and elephant in one week

    Yala, Mirissa and Udawalawe sit within three hours of each other on the south coast.

    Land

    Fly into Colombo (CMB). Apply for the ETA only at eta.gov.lk: it is free for 40 nationalities since May 2026, and copycat sites still charge.

    Ride

    The Ella line runs again between Nanu Oya and Badulla. Kandy to Nanu Oya is still closed after Cyclone Ditwah, so go by road to Nanu Oya and board there.

    Climb

    Every great view here is a dawn view. Gates open about 7:00; mist and heat take the hills by 10:00.

    Watch

    Pick parks by season, not fame: Yala and Wilpattu for leopard, Minneriya for the July Gathering, Kumana and Gal Oya when the east is dry.

    Wade

    Two monsoons, two beach seasons: the south and west from December to April, the east from April to September. Swim only where locals do.

    Before you fly

    Do I need a visa?

    Every visitor needs an Electronic Travel Authorisation before arrival. Since 25 May 2026 it is free for nationals of 40 countries; others pay the official fee. Apply only at eta.gov.lk. It allows 30 days with double entry and can be extended in Colombo.

    When should I go?

    There is always a coast in season. December to April: the south, west and hills. April to September: the east coast and the north. October and November are the wettest island-wide, but quiet and green. Use the month dial on this page to see it.

    Is it safe after the cyclone?

    Cyclone Ditwah hit in November 2025. Roads to the main sights reopened within weeks and tourism is running normally. The Kandy–Nanu Oya rail section is still being rebuilt (expected 2027); everything else on this site is open. Allow extra time on hill roads.

    How do I get around?

    A car with a driver is the most common choice for a loop (about US$50–70 a day plus the driver's stay). Trains are cheap and scenic; book reserved seats at the station or the official Sri Lanka Railways site. In towns, use the PickMe or Uber apps for metered tuk-tuks.

    Cash or card?

    Cards work in hotels and bigger restaurants. Carry rupees for tuk-tuks, temples, village guides and park jeeps. ATMs are everywhere except the remote villages (Meemure, Delft). Prices for foreigners at sites are set in US dollars and charged in rupees.

    What should I wear to temples?

    Shoulders and knees covered, shoes and hats off. Never pose with your back to a Buddha image, and do not show Buddha tattoos. At Hindu kovils in the north, men remove their shirts.

    Who do I call in an emergency?

    Police 119. Ambulance 1990 (free, island-wide). Tourism hotline 1912. Save these before you land; they work from any phone.
